notes: Six printed labels, six turns: the swearing-in of Cafiero as vicepresidente and of Genoud as presidente provisional. The identical stenographer line '-Puestos de pie los señores senadores y el público:' is printed twice, once before each oath, and I listed it twice — it is two separate printed paragraphs, not a duplication error on my part. The '(Aplausos.)' in the chair's third and sixth turns sits inside the speech paragraph, so by rule 4 it is not an event. Both of those turns run on into an unlabelled indented line kept inside the same turn ('Invito al señor senador José Genoud a acercarse al estrado...' and 'Como se ha cumplido con el objetivo propuesto, queda concluida esta sesión preparatoria.'). Typographic point worth flagging: the fourth label is printed with NO space after its terminator — 'Sr. PRESIDENTE.-Señor senador José Genoud:' — whereas every other label on the page has one. I verified this at high magnification; the label itself is unchanged, so I recorded it as 'Sr. PRESIDENTE.-'. In the first turn the colon after 'Cafiero' is set bold like the label, while the parallel colon after 'Genoud' in the fourth turn is not. The chair is printed without a surname throughout. The signature of the Director del Cuerpo de Taquígrafos closes the provisional version and is furniture, not speech; below it the bottom third of the page is blank.
